Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0033", "row_sha256": "e5ce2c42fcd8eee6e4b98e6aa8dcfff9080d633cc6839996b49c722be90bf992", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "okay i need a prompt for one member-facing piece about the shared bicycle shed at alder court, not a decision memo and not an update that pretends we know more than we do. the shed is behind the laundry room, and people enter from the paved path beside the bins. this is about what to do with the bikes during the next stage after the floor-drain work, not about the repair itself. please make the requested action depend on the inspection record, because nobody in the residents group has confirmed what it says yet. the main thing i want is a notice asking people to move their bikes, but only if the required check is actually documented. if it is not, i still need something useful rather than a blank answer: a maintenance request asking for the missing inspection or clarification. those are alternatives, not two pieces to write together.

The detail that decides which piece to draft is the caretaker’s signed inspection sheet dated 14 May. The condition is met only if that sheet records both that the two anchor plates on the north wall passed the pull test and that both shed doors latch properly. If either item is missing from the sheet, if the test is recorded as failed, or if the sheet cannot be located, use the other route. Please don’t treat somebody remembering a conversation as the signed record, and don’t say the test passed unless the sheet says it did. The residents group has asked me to keep this distinction clear because two different versions of the inspection have been mentioned in passing, and no one has supplied a copy.

If the condition is met, write the member notice asking users to move bicycles now kept at the temporary south-side rail to the north-wall rack by 22 May. The south rail has six spaces and was installed temporarily while the drain work was under way. It is still standing, but it is not supposed to be presented as the normal long-term location. The north-wall rack has ten hoops and is intended to hold twenty ordinary bicycles. Don’t turn that into a claim that every kind of bicycle will fit, or promise that an individual space has been reserved. The notice should say what action is requested and the date, without making it sound like a warning or claiming that anyone has already agreed.

A little background for whichever route you take: Alder Court has 28 households, and the shed is shared by residents rather than assigned to individual flats. The drain work finished on 8 May, according to the contractor’s note on the noticeboard. That fact alone does not establish that the wall anchors or doors passed inspection. The caretaker has not sent the residents group a copy of the 14 May sheet. The key to the shed is held at the building office, but don’t include key collection arrangements in the member notice; that is not part of this move request. The current question is limited to the south rail and the north-wall rack, not the bicycle room in the basement, which is a separate space.

If the sheet does not meet the full condition, write a short maintenance request to the property manager asking them to provide the signed inspection sheet or arrange the relevant check, and to clarify the status of both anchor plates and both doors. Make that a request, not a statement that a defect has been found. We don’t know whether the sheet was misplaced, whether one detail was left off it, or whether the inspection is incomplete. Do not ask the manager to approve a move on behalf of residents, and do not add a new deadline for the inspection. This fallback is useful because the residents need a verifiable answer before the notice asking people to move bikes can be sent.

There are a few practical details that may help with the wording, but please don’t let them change the condition. The north rack is on the wall opposite the entrance, near the small window; the south rail is beside the floor drain. The blue cargo bike is currently at the south rail. The coordinator said, “please leave the blue cargo bike where it is until we know what the wall can carry.” Keep that quote as background rather than turning it into a separate instruction to a named owner. In particular, don’t say the cargo bike must move by 22 May, since the request is about bicycles generally and there has been no confirmation that it fits the north rack.

1. Choose exactly one route by checking the signed sheet against both parts of the condition.
2. Under the first route, draft the notice with the move request and 22 May date; under the other route, draft the maintenance request described above.
3. Keep the writing plain and suitable for residents or the property manager, as appropriate. Avoid blame, invented inspection results, and a claim that the residents group has approved anything.

The drain contractor is due to collect the temporary barrier on 20 May, but that collection is not the same thing as permission to remove the south rail, and no one has asked for a rail-removal instruction. Please do not add one. The residents group will decide separately what to do with the rail after the inspection information is available. Return only the single piece of text selected by the condition, with no explanation, heading about which route was chosen, or note to me. If the record is unavailable or does not affirm both required checks, use the maintenance-request route; do not draft the move notice as a precaution.", "output": "Create one member-facing piece of text about the shared bicycle shed at Alder Court. Choose exactly one of the following routes, based on the caretaker’s signed inspection sheet dated 14 May:

- **If the sheet records both that the two north-wall anchor plates passed the pull test and that both shed doors latch properly:** Draft a notice asking users to move bicycles currently kept at the temporary south-side rail to the north-wall rack by 22 May.
- **Otherwise:** Draft a short maintenance request to the property manager asking them to provide the signed inspection sheet or arrange the relevant check, and to clarify the status of both anchor plates and both doors. Use this route if either detail is missing, the test is recorded as failed, or the sheet cannot be located. Do not draft the move notice as a precaution.

Write only the selected piece, not both alternatives. Do not treat a remembered conversation as the signed record or say the test passed unless the sheet records that result. The residents group has heard two versions of the inspection but has not received a copy, and has not approved anything.

Alder Court has 28 households. The shed is shared by residents, is behind the laundry room, and is entered from the paved path beside the bins. The north-wall rack, opposite the entrance near the small window, has ten hoops and is intended to hold twenty ordinary bicycles. The temporary south-side rail, beside the floor drain, has six spaces and was installed while drain work was under way. The contractor’s noticeboard note says the drain work finished on 8 May. This does not establish that the anchors or doors passed inspection. The rail is still standing, but do not present it as the normal long-term location. Do not claim every kind of bicycle will fit the north rack or that any individual space is reserved.

For the notice route, state the requested action and the 22 May date without making it sound like a warning or saying anyone has already agreed. The blue cargo bike is currently at the south rail. The coordinator said, “please leave the blue cargo bike where it is until we know what the wall can carry.” Treat this as background, not as a separate instruction to a named owner. Do not say the cargo bike must move by 22 May; the request concerns bicycles generally, and it has not been confirmed that the cargo bike fits the north rack.

For the maintenance-request route, make a request, not a statement that a defect has been found. It is not known whether the sheet was misplaced, a detail was left off it, or the inspection is incomplete. Do not ask the property manager to approve a move on residents’ behalf or add a new deadline for the inspection. The residents need a verifiable answer before a move notice can be sent.

The shed key is held at the building office, but do not include key-collection arrangements. The basement bicycle room is separate and is outside the scope of this request. The drain contractor is due to collect the temporary barrier on 20 May; that does not mean the south rail should be removed, and no rail-removal instruction has been requested. The residents group will decide separately what to do with the rail after the inspection information is available.

Use plain, appropriate wording for residents or the property manager, depending on the selected route. Return only the single selected piece of text, with no explanation, route heading, or note to the requester."}]
